sources.title: ARP6983 / ED-324 – Development and Assurance guidelines for Aeronautical Systems and Equipment Implemented with Machine Learning (FAA AI/ML Technical Exchange Meeting presentation, August 2025)
sources.publisher: SAE G-34 / EUROCAE WG-114 (presented at FAA AI/ML Technical Exchange)
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public 16-slide read-only presentation. Inspected committee history, the statement-of-concerns gap slide, issue 1 scope, system-level safety approach and schedule. The deck states it is based on Draft 7 (work in progress) and is subject to change; SAE copyright prohibits redistribution, so only short quotations are recorded.

regions.excerpt: Created in 2019 ... ER-022 / AIR6988 (Statement of concerns) Published on 30 April 2021 ... ED-324 / ARP6983 ... Publication targeted for June 2026
Issue 1 limited to a subset of ML technologies ... Non-adaptive ML in supervised mode, and up to DAL C / AL 3 / SWAL 2

regions.locator: Slides 11-12, how the ARP addresses safety at the system level
regions.excerpt: the ARP cannot be used if the outcome is higher than IDAL C/AL3/SWAL2
SAE Ballot 1 ended on April 7th, ≈1800 comments are being addressed ... Issue 2 will follow, covering more ML techniques (such as Reinforcement Learning)

sources.limitations: A committee presentation of a draft (Draft 7, WIP), not the standard. Scope and schedule were stated as subject to change; the EUROCAE status page captured 2026-09-16 (C-CHAL-005) shows a later target date. Copyrighted by SAE; not redistributed.

sources.title: NPA 2025-07 — Detailed specifications and associated AMC and GM, Artificial intelligence trustworthiness (landing page)
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public EASA landing page and inspected its dates and summary.

regions.locator: NPA 2025-07 landing page summary and dates
regions.excerpt: proposes a new set of detailed specifications on artificial intelligence (AI) trustworthiness for the safe use of AI in aviation in response to Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the Artificial Intelligence Act)

sources.limitations: A rulemaking landing page for proposed material; it does not establish adoption. See C-STD-002 for the captured comment-response status.

sources.title: Certification of Safety-Critical Software Under DO-178C and DO-278A (history and verification regions)
sources.jurisdiction: Public explanation of airborne software assurance
sources.inspection_scope: Retained public NASA PDF (sister-project capture) and inspected the introduction/history, software levels and coverage, and tool-qualification sections. Same originating document as S-BASE-002; recorded separately for the history and level/tool regions.

regions.locator: Section I introduction and history, pp. 1-2
regions.excerpt: DO-178B was a derivative product of DO-178A, DO-178, and other documents and was released in December 1992.

regions.locator: Section III.A Software Levels and Coverage, p. 3
regions.excerpt: Since testing can never prove the absence of software errors, the primary DO-178C philosophy is to demonstrate the quality of the software development process
DO-178C sets forth five tool qualification levels (TQL-1 – TQL-5) based on the software level

sources.limitations: NASA's public explanatory paper, not the licensed standard; it supports manager-level characterization and dates only.

sources.title: Incorporating international rules into GB type approval for road vehicles – outcome
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public GOV.UK outcome page and inspected the UN Regulation 157 (ALKS) question, response summary and government decision.

regions.locator: Outcome page, UN Regulation 157 question and decision
regions.excerpt: mandating compliance with the requirements of UNECE Regulation 157 on ALKS ... As contracting parties to UN Regulation 157, there is an obligation on the UK to accept approvals.

sources.limitations: A UK government decision about GB type approval; it describes UN Regulation 157 as an international type-approval regulation but is not the regulation text and does not establish EU or US practice.

sources.title: Automated Lane Keeping Systems (ALKS) and Listing of Self-Driving Vehicles
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public VCA page and inspected its ALKS description and R157 listing-review process.

regions.locator: ALKS description and R157 listing review
regions.excerpt: Vehicles which are approved to UNECE R157 and include the United Kingdom within their Operational Design Domain (ODD) should meet the threshold of self-driving

sources.limitations: UK agency guidance for listing; not the R157 text, not an EU/UNECE-wide statement, and not a safety finding about any vehicle.
